title: The Miraculousness And Testimony Of The Quran 17th Degree The Impossibility Of Producing Its Like In View Of Source Addressee And Purpose

questions.question: According to the passage, what three things help show the worth and excellence of any speech?
questions.answer: Its source, its audience, and its purpose.

questions.question: Why does the passage say no other speech can match the Qur'an?
questions.answer: Because it comes from the Lord of all creation, speaks to the greatest messenger on behalf of all beings, and explains the deepest truths about life, creation, and the Hereafter.

questions.question: How is the speaker of the Qur'an described?
questions.answer: As the Sustainer of all worlds and the Creator of the entire universe.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the style of this divine address?
questions.answer: It says the speech is completely free from copying and artificial performance.

questions.question: Who is the main addressee described in the passage?
questions.answer: The messenger sent in the name of all people, and even all beings.

questions.question: What is said about the addressee’s faith and its impact?
questions.answer: His faith was vast and powerful, and it became the cause for the rise of Islam.

questions.question: What does the passage say the Qur'an explains about this life and the next?
questions.answer: It explains the matters that lead to happiness in both worlds.

questions.question: Besides happiness in both worlds, what else does the Qur'an explain about the universe?
questions.answer: It explains why the universe was created and the divine purposes within it.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the belief of the one addressed by the Qur'an?
questions.answer: It presents his belief as the highest and widest in scope, carrying all the truths of Islam.

questions.question: Which comparisons are used to show how the Qur'an presents the universe?
questions.answer: It is compared to showing the universe like a map, a clock, or a house.

questions.question: Why is the Qur'an’s explanation of the universe described as unique?
questions.answer: Because it teaches creation in the way only its Maker can truly explain it.

questions.question: What conclusion is drawn from that unique way of explaining the universe?
questions.answer: That producing anything equal to the Qur'an is impossible.

questions.question: What does the passage say many highly intelligent scholars have done in relation to the Qur'an?
questions.answer: They have written detailed commentaries to explain and prove its many qualities, meanings, secrets, and signs.

questions.question: How large are some of these commentaries said to be?
questions.answer: Some are said to be thirty, forty, or even seventy volumes long.

questions.question: What kinds of things do these scholarly works bring out from the Qur'an?
questions.answer: They bring out its qualities, subtle points, special features, hidden meanings, and signs related to unseen matters.

questions.question: What special role is given to the Risale-i Nur in this passage?
questions.answer: It is presented as a collection whose many parts each prove a particular quality or truth of the Qur'an with strong arguments.

questions.question: What is the main point of mentioning works about technology, signs, and unseen matters from the Risale-i Nur?
questions.answer: To show that different parts of it uncover different lights and truths from the Qur'an.

questions.question: What final conclusion does the passage reach from all these explanations and proofs?
questions.answer: That the Qur'an has no equal, is miraculous and wondrous, and is the speech of the One who knows the unseen.

questions.question: What basic principle about speech is stated at the start of the passage?
questions.answer: To judge a speech properly, you need to know who said it, who it is for, and why it was said.

questions.question: Using that principle, what judgment is made about the Qur'an?
questions.answer: That nothing can equal it or rise to its level.

questions.question: What makes the Qur'an’s origin so important in this argument?
questions.answer: It is presented as coming from the Lord and Creator of everything.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the Qur'an as communication rather than just a text?
questions.answer: It describes it as a direct address and conversation.

questions.question: What does the passage deny about the Qur'an’s manner of expression?
questions.answer: It denies that it contains imitation or fake display.

questions.question: In whose name is the one addressed by the Qur'an sent?
questions.answer: In the name of all humanity, and even all beings.

questions.question: What result came from the breadth and strength of this person’s belief?
questions.answer: It led to the emergence of the great religion of Islam.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest about the spiritual rank of the one addressed?
questions.answer: It presents him as raised to an extremely high nearness and honor.

questions.question: What major subjects does the Qur'an explain according to the passage?
questions.answer: It explains true success in both worlds, the outcomes of creation, and the divine wisdom within the universe.

questions.question: How does the Qur'an relate to the faith of the one it addresses?
questions.answer: It lays out and explains his complete and far-reaching belief.

questions.question: Why are the examples of a map, a clock, and a house used?
questions.answer: To show that the Qur'an presents the universe as something ordered, meaningful, and understandable.

questions.question: According to the passage, who can describe the universe in the fullest way?
questions.answer: The One who made it.

questions.question: What inference does the passage ask the reader to make from that fact?
questions.answer: That human beings cannot produce speech equal to the Qur'an’s explanation.

questions.question: What do the many detailed Qur'an commentaries show?
questions.answer: They show that the Qur'an contains countless layers of meaning and proof.

questions.question: What do the lengths of some commentaries suggest about the Qur'an?
questions.answer: They suggest that its meanings are deep, rich, and not exhausted easily.

questions.question: What is said about the individual sections of the Risale-i Nur?
questions.answer: Each section is said to reveal and prove one particular light or truth from the Qur'an.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention examples involving civilization, electricity, and unseen news?
questions.answer: To show the wide range of insights scholars have drawn from the Qur'an.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the Qur'an at the end in relation to the unseen world?
questions.answer: As the expression of the unseen realm within the visible world and as the word of the All-Knowing.

questions.question: What does the passage say must be known before the value of speech can be understood?
questions.answer: The speaker, the intended audience, and the aim of the speech.

questions.question: How does that idea support the claim that the Qur'an is beyond comparison?
questions.answer: Because its speaker, audience, and purpose are unmatched in greatness.

questions.question: What is the significance of the Qur'an coming from the Lord of all worlds?
questions.answer: It means the speech has the highest possible source and authority.

questions.question: How is the Qur'an different from ordinary human speech in style?
questions.answer: It is presented as natural and genuine, not copied or forced.

questions.question: Why is the identity of the one addressed important to the argument?
questions.answer: Because he represents all humanity and all beings, so the message is addressed at the highest level.

questions.question: What effect did the addressee’s faith have in history, according to the passage?
questions.answer: It became the basis for the rise and strength of Islam.

questions.question: What does the passage include among the Qur'an’s main teachings?
questions.answer: It includes guidance about well-being in this life and the next.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the Qur'an’s explanation of creation?
questions.answer: It explains the outcomes and purposes placed within creation.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the belief carried by the one addressed?
questions.answer: As the broadest and loftiest belief, containing all Islamic truths.

questions.question: What do the images of the map, clock, and house help the reader understand?
questions.answer: That the universe is shown as ordered and meaningful, and the Qur'an explains its structure and function clearly.

questions.question: Why would matching the Qur'an be impossible, according to the passage?
questions.answer: Because no one can explain the universe as perfectly as its Creator.

questions.question: What kind of scholars are mentioned in the second paragraph?
questions.answer: Very intelligent and exact scholars who wrote careful commentaries on the Qur'an.

questions.question: What do those scholars prove through evidence and argument?
questions.answer: They prove the Qur'an’s many qualities, subtleties, deep meanings, and signs.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the number and size of these scholarly works?
questions.answer: It says there are many of them, and some extend to dozens of volumes.

questions.question: How is the Risale-i Nur presented within this scholarly tradition?
questions.answer: As a special collection in which each part demonstrates a distinct feature or truth of the Qur'an.

questions.question: What is the purpose of listing several parts of the Risale-i Nur?
questions.answer: To give examples of how different sections uncover different dimensions of the Qur'an.

questions.question: What overall “stamp” do all these commentaries and examples provide?
questions.answer: They serve as confirming proof that the Qur'an is unmatched and miraculous.

questions.question: What two final descriptions summarize the Qur'an’s nature at the end of the passage?
questions.answer: It is described as a marvel without equal and as divine speech connected to the unseen.

questions.question: At the beginning of the passage, what standard is given for judging how great a speech is?
questions.answer: You judge it by considering its speaker, its listener, and its goal.

questions.question: Based on that standard, what claim is made about the Qur'an?
questions.answer: That no similar speech can be produced.

questions.question: What description of Allah in the passage strengthens this claim?
questions.answer: The Qur'an is said to come from the Lord of every world and the Maker of the whole universe.

questions.question: What does the passage mean by saying the Qur'an shows no sign of imitation?
questions.answer: It means its expression is original and not borrowed from anyone else.

questions.question: How broad is the mission of the one addressed by the Qur'an?
questions.answer: It reaches beyond a single group to all people and even all beings.

questions.question: What does the passage connect to the rise of Islam?
questions.answer: The power and wide reach of the addressee’s faith.

questions.question: What does the Qur'an explain about human life?
questions.answer: It explains what leads to true success in this world and the next.

questions.question: What does it explain about the universe itself?
questions.answer: It explains the results of creation and the divine purposes within it.

questions.question: How is the faith of the one addressed described?
questions.answer: As the highest and most comprehensive faith.

questions.question: What do the three examples of a map, clock, and house have in common?
questions.answer: They are all organized things that can be understood when shown by the one who designed them.

questions.question: What point is made by comparing the universe to those things?
questions.answer: That the Qur'an explains the universe with the insight of its Maker.

questions.question: What conclusion follows from that comparison?
questions.answer: Human beings cannot bring forth something equal to the Qur'an.

questions.question: What evidence from scholarship is given in support of the Qur'an’s uniqueness?
questions.answer: Many learned scholars have written extensive commentaries that uncover countless meanings and proofs in it.

questions.question: What kinds of matters do these commentaries discuss?
questions.answer: They discuss qualities, subtle meanings, special features, hidden truths, and signs related to unseen realities.

questions.question: Why is the Risale-i Nur singled out in the passage?
questions.answer: Because its many sections are presented as clear demonstrations of separate Qur'anic truths and wonders.

questions.question: What does the passage show by giving examples from different treatises of the Risale-i Nur?
questions.answer: That the Qur'an contains guidance and signs across many subjects and levels of understanding.

questions.question: What does each part of the Risale-i Nur contribute, according to the passage?
questions.answer: Each one reveals a distinct truth or light from the Qur'an.

questions.question: What final proof is drawn from all of this scholarly effort?
questions.answer: That the Qur'an has no equal, is miraculous, and is divine speech from the Knower of the unseen.

questions.question: What three questions should be asked in order to understand the quality of a speech, according to the passage?
questions.answer: Who said it, who received it, and what it was meant to accomplish.

questions.question: After applying those questions to the Qur'an, what verdict does the passage give?
questions.answer: That nothing comparable to it can be reached.

questions.question: How is the source of the Qur'an presented?
questions.answer: As the Lord of all existence and the Creator of the universe.

questions.question: What does the passage emphasize about the Qur'an’s tone and form?
questions.answer: That it is a real divine address, not something copied or artificially made.

questions.question: Who is the Qur'an directed to in the passage?
questions.answer: To the messenger who represents all human beings and all creation.

questions.question: What historical effect of the messenger’s faith is mentioned?
questions.answer: It brought forth the powerful civilization and religion of Islam.

questions.question: What areas of human concern does the Qur'an address?
questions.answer: It addresses happiness in this life and the next.

questions.question: What larger cosmic questions does it also address?
questions.answer: It addresses why the universe was created and what divine purposes are at work in it.

questions.question: How does the passage characterize the messenger’s belief?
questions.answer: As the most complete and far-reaching belief.

questions.question: Why does the passage use everyday objects like a house and a clock in speaking about the universe?
questions.answer: To make clear that the universe has order and meaning and can be explained by its Maker.

questions.question: According to the passage, why can people not produce something like the Qur'an?
questions.answer: Because they cannot explain the whole universe from the standpoint of the One who created it.

questions.question: What does the passage say thousands of scholars have done?
questions.answer: They have written detailed explanations of the Qur'an and shown many of its evidences and subtleties.

questions.question: What does the existence of such large commentaries suggest about the Qur'an?
questions.answer: That it contains immense depth and many layers of meaning.

questions.question: What is one reason the passage mentions works of thirty to seventy volumes?
questions.answer: To show the richness of the Qur'an and the great effort needed to uncover its meanings.

questions.question: How is the Risale-i Nur described in relation to the Qur'an?
questions.answer: As a set of writings in which each section proves a particular aspect of the Qur'an.

questions.question: What is the purpose of mentioning examples from different treatises in that collection?
questions.answer: To illustrate that different sections draw out different signs, wisdoms, and wonders from the Qur'an.

questions.question: What does the phrase about a “stamp confirming” mean in this passage?
questions.answer: It means these works act like strong proof that the Qur'an’s qualities are real.

questions.question: Summarize the passage’s final view of the Qur'an in one sentence.
questions.answer: It presents the Qur'an as an unmatched miracle and as divine speech that brings truths from the unseen into the visible world.

questions.question: What rule for evaluating speech is given at the start of the target passage?
questions.answer: A speech is best understood by looking at its speaker, its hearer, and its purpose.

questions.question: What conclusion does the passage draw about the Qur'an after applying that rule?
questions.answer: That it has no equal and cannot be matched.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the one who speaks the Qur'an?
questions.answer: He is the Lord of all worlds and the Creator of everything.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the Qur'an as speech?
questions.answer: As a true divine address that contains no trace of imitation or pretended style.

questions.question: Who is described as receiving this address?
questions.answer: The messenger sent on behalf of all people and all beings.

questions.question: What two things are said about this messenger’s standing?
questions.answer: He is the most renowned among humanity, and his powerful faith gave rise to Islam.

questions.question: What does the Qur'an teach about human destiny?
questions.answer: It teaches what leads to success in this world and in the Hereafter.

questions.question: What does it teach about the universe?
questions.answer: It teaches the outcomes of its creation and the divine purposes within it.

questions.question: How does the passage present the messenger’s faith as related to the Qur'an’s message?
questions.answer: His faith is shown as the fullest expression of the truths that the Qur'an sets out.

questions.question: What is the effect of comparing the universe to a map, a clock, and a house?
questions.answer: It helps the reader see that the universe is arranged with order and can be explained clearly by its Maker.

questions.question: Why does the passage say producing something like the Qur'an is impossible?
questions.answer: Because such a complete explanation of creation can only come from the One who created it.

questions.question: What kind of evidence is added in the second paragraph?
questions.answer: The testimony of many expert scholars through their detailed commentaries.

questions.question: What do these scholars uncover in the Qur'an?
questions.answer: Countless qualities, fine meanings, distinguishing features, secrets, and signs about unseen matters.

questions.question: Why is the number of volumes in some commentaries important?
questions.answer: It shows how much depth and richness scholars have found in the Qur'an.

questions.question: How does the passage portray the Risale-i Nur?
questions.answer: As a body of writings whose parts each establish one specific truth or aspect of the Qur'an.

questions.question: What do the examples from the Risale-i Nur reveal about Qur'anic interpretation?
questions.answer: They show that the Qur'an can be studied for guidance on many subjects and at many levels.

questions.question: What repeated idea is emphasized by saying each part shows one truth or one light?
questions.answer: That the Qur'an contains many separate yet connected dimensions of guidance and wonder.

questions.question: What final titles or descriptions are given to the Qur'an at the end of the passage?
questions.answer: It is called an unequaled miracle, a marvel, the voice of the unseen in the visible world, and the word of the One who knows the unseen.
